text:
Jake DeBrusk's season has two stories, and the louder one isn't about his play. Reports this month (Markerzone, Vancouver Hockey Daily) say his stance hasn't changed: he doesn't want to be part of a Canucks rebuild. On a team with seven points in 19 games, that question isn't going away.

On the ice he has been one of Vancouver's better forwards, quietly. He has 10 points in 17 games, and the Canucks are much better with him than without him by the chances (about seven points of expected goal share better). His finishing is a little behind, five goals on 6.4 expected, and Yahoo Sports wondered aloud whether he's due for one of his hot streaks. Our range says 19 to 32 goals over a full season, which fits the 23 he scored last year.

Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking explains his game: 55% of his shots come off the rush, so he does his damage in the seconds after a turnover. Evolving-Hockey had him around replacement level last season, but against top-6% competition and with weak linemates. If Vancouver sells, he's the kind of winger contenders call about.
headline: DeBrusk's play, and his stance
